Q5647.L1t: Ugg boots are woollen-lined sheepskin footwear that originated in Australia.
Q5647.L2t: Shane Stedman made his first sheepskin boots in 1973 and sold the rights to the US company Deckers in 1983.
Q5647.L3t: Stedman said that making the brand a world leader would mean moving to the US, which he refused to do because he would never give up Sydney and surfing, so he let the rights go without regret.
Q5647.L4t: The text mainly shows that the inventor willingly gave up a possible fortune so he could keep his life in Sydney and his surfing.
Q5647.L2f: Stedman sold the rights to Deckers in 1995 for a lump sum of one million pounds.
Q5647.L3f: The passage is chiefly about the purpose behind the boots' creation, which was to serve the surfing community alone, and the sale of the rights is only a minor detail.
Q5647.L4f: The text mainly tells us that the boots were created with surfers specifically in mind.

Q5649.L1t: Catheter valves are used with urinary catheters as an alternative to a drainage bag.
Q5649.L2t: A catheter valve is a tap-like device fitted to the end of a catheter that lets the bladder fill and then be emptied at intervals.
Q5649.L3t: A valve works by letting the bladder fill and then releasing urine at intervals, but just after surgery the bladder usually needs to stay continuously drained.
Q5649.L4t: A catheter valve would not be used for a patient who has just had surgery.
Q5649.L2f: Catheter valves are single-use devices that have to be replaced every day.
Q5649.L3f: A catheter valve is suited only to situations where urine volumes are being recorded, because the valve itself tracks the amount passed.
Q5649.L4f: You would avoid a catheter valve when there is no requirement to measure urine output.

Q8537.L1t: Philosophers of law debate both what punishment is and whether it can be morally justified.
Q8537.L2t: Definitions of punishment typically describe an authority deliberately inflicting unpleasant consequences on someone for an offence.
Q8537.L3t: If a moral justification were built into the definition, any argument over whether punishment is justified would be settled in advance by definition, so the definition must not presuppose any moral stance.
Q8537.L4t: Separating them matters so that the definition stays neutral on values, leaving moral justification to be argued as a separate question.
Q8537.L2f: The concept of punishment is generally agreed to have been fixed by Kant in a single, uncontested formulation.
Q8537.L3f: The reason for the separation is that punishment as an actual social institution runs independently of any moral reasons offered for it, so the two must not be run together.
Q8537.L4f: The separation matters because, in reality, the institution of punishment exists apart from any justification given for it.
